cues.title: 气体离开，固体一定变轻吗？
cues.titleEn: Gas leaves. Must the solid get lighter?
cues.caption: 气体离开了，固体会怎样？
cues.captionEn: Gas leaves. What happens to the solid?
cues.zh: 铁粉与水蒸气反应后，管内留下黑色固体，导出的气体具有可燃性。有东西跑掉了，固体就一定变轻吗？沿着装置看：湿棉花中的水成为蒸气，先到达热铁，再通向气体观察处。先别急着看答案，我们跟住水中的一个氧。
cues.en: After iron reacts with steam, a black solid remains and the departing gas is combustible. If something escapes, must the solid become lighter? Follow the apparatus: water from the damp cotton becomes steam, reaches the hot iron, then flows toward the gas observation. Before revealing the answer, follow an oxygen atom from water.

cues.title: 同一份水，分成两条去向
cues.caption: 氧留进固体，氢组成气体。
cues.captionEn: Oxygen joins the solid; hydrogen forms gas.
cues.zh: 把反应区放大成一张净变化图：三份铁与四份水，共有三个铁、四个氧和八个氢。盯住带光环的氧，它从水的一侧移到固体的一侧；另外三个氧也留下。八个氢则两两组成四份氢气。四氧化三铁表示固体的组成，不是一个孤立的小分子。原子没有消失，它们重新组合了。
cues.en: Zoom into a net account of the reaction region. Three iron atoms and four water units contain three iron, four oxygen and eight hydrogen atoms. Follow the highlighted oxygen from the water side into the solid. The other three oxygens also stay. Eight hydrogens pair into four hydrogen molecules. Magnetite’s formula describes the solid’s composition, not a separate little molecule. No atom disappears; the atoms are rearranged.

cues.title: 增重从哪里来？
cues.titleEn: Where does the extra solid mass come from?
cues.caption: 固体增加的质量，来自水中的氧。
cues.captionEn: The extra solid mass comes from oxygen in water.
cues.zh: 现在把同一关系放大成一克铁的计量算例。水足够、铁完全转化时，黑色固体约一点三八二克，多出的零点三八二克来自水中的氧。生成的氢气离开固体，但它的质量仍在总账里。没有反应完的水也要留下来。称量范围不同，读数会不同；把所有物质放回总账，质量始终对得上。
cues.en: Scale the same relation to an illustrative one gram of iron. With enough water and complete iron conversion, the solid is about 1.382 grams. Its extra 0.382 grams comes from oxygen in water. Hydrogen leaves the solid, but its mass remains in the total account. Any unreacted water also remains. Different weighing boundaries give different readings; counting every substance preserves the total mass.

cues.title: 气泡能证明什么？
cues.caption: 气泡说明有气体经过，还要结合其他证据。
cues.captionEn: Bubbles show gas passage; other evidence is needed.
cues.zh: 回到气体观察处。气泡只说明有气体经过，空气也能形成气泡。教材还给出可燃性检验，再结合反应物和产物的分析，支持氢气生成。黑色也不是四氧化三铁独有的颜色。我们用一组相互支持的证据解释反应，不能让一个气泡或一种颜色包办鉴定。
cues.en: Return to the gas observation. A bubble only shows gas passage; air can make bubbles too. The textbook also shows a combustibility test. Together with the reactants and products, that supports hydrogen formation. Black is not unique to magnetite either. The explanation rests on several supporting observations, not a single bubble or colour.

cues.title: 水加倍，产氢也加倍吗？
cues.titleEn: Twice the water, twice the hydrogen?
cues.caption: 先找出哪一种反应物先用完。
cues.captionEn: First find which reactant runs out.
cues.zh: 两份算例都用一克铁。一份有零点三克水，另一份把水加倍到零点六克，氢气也会加倍吗？先暂停想一想。第一份水先用完，还有铁留下；第二份却是铁先用完，仍有水剩余。氢气分别约十六点六五和二十三点八八毫摩尔，并没有加倍。多给水不能弥补已经用完的铁，这就是限量反应物的作用。
cues.en: Both examples use one gram of iron. One has 0.3 grams of water; the other doubles it to 0.6 grams. Will hydrogen also double? Pause and predict. In the first, water runs out and iron remains. In the second, iron runs out and water remains. Hydrogen amounts are about 16.65 and 23.88 millimoles, not double. More water cannot replace iron that has already been consumed. That is the role of the limiting reactant.

question.zh: 气体离开，固体为什么会增重？
question.en: Why can the solid gain mass as gas leaves?

lead.zh: 跟住水中的氧，再预测水加倍后的产氢量。
lead.en: Follow oxygen from water, then predict the yield when water doubles.

principle.zh: 水中的氧加入固体、氢组成 H₂；所有物质一起守恒，最先耗尽的反应物限制产量。
principle.en: Oxygen from water joins the solid while hydrogen forms H₂. The complete material account is conserved, and the reactant that runs out limits yield.

question.zh: 同样 1 g 铁，水从 0.3 g 增至 0.6 g，理想产氢量会加倍吗？
question.en: With 1 g of iron, does increasing water from 0.3 g to 0.6 g double ideal hydrogen yield?

explanation.zh: 不会。前者水限量，约 16.65 mmol H₂ 且余铁；后者铁限量，约 23.88 mmol H₂ 且余水。
explanation.en: No. Water limits the first case to about 16.65 mmol H₂, leaving iron. Iron limits the second to about 23.88 mmol H₂, leaving water.
